What to Do After a Motorcycle Accident

Knowing the right steps after an accident reduces stress and protects your legal position. Read our Best Motorcycle Roads in Scotland: 15 Must-Ride Routes guide for more. Read our Motorcycle Helmet Safety Ratings Explained guide for more. Read our Motorcycle Hand Signals Every Rider Should Know guide for more.

  1. Stop and Assess — Turn off engine, check yourself for injuries.
  2. Call 999 — If anyone is injured or the road is blocked.
  3. Don't Remove Helmets — Never remove an injured rider's helmet unless they cannot breathe.
  4. Exchange Details — Name, address, insurance, registration with all parties.
  5. Photograph Everything — Damage, road conditions, vehicle positions, weather.
  6. Get Witnesses — Names and contact details of any witnesses.
  7. Report to Police — Required within 24 hours if details not exchanged or someone was injured.
  8. Contact Insurer — Report the accident as soon as possible.
Important: Never admit fault at the scene. State facts only.
keyTakeaways: Stop, turn off the engine and check yourself for injuries before anything else.
Call 999 if anyone is injured or the road is blocked.
Never remove an injured rider's helmet unless they cannot breathe.
Photograph damage, road conditions, vehicle positions and gather witness details.
Report to the police within 24 hours if details were not exchanged or someone was hurt.

faq.q: What is the first thing to do after a motorcycle accident?
faq.a: Stop, turn off your engine to reduce fire risk, and check yourself for injuries before moving. If it is safe, get clear of traffic. Only then assess others involved. Staying calm and methodical protects your safety and your legal position. Call 999 immediately if anyone is injured or the carriageway is blocked.

faq.q: Should I remove an injured rider's helmet?
faq.a: No, never remove an injured rider's helmet unless they cannot breathe. Moving the head risks worsening a spinal injury. Leave it to trained paramedics, who know how to do it safely if required. Instead, keep the casualty still, reassure them, and wait for the emergency services to arrive.

faq.q: When must I report a motorcycle accident to the police?
faq.a: In the UK you must report an accident to the police within 24 hours if you did not exchange details at the scene, or if anyone was injured. Even where details were exchanged, reporting is wise if there is any dispute. Contact your insurer as soon as possible regardless, as most policies require prompt notification.

faq.q: What evidence should I gather at the scene?
faq.a: Photograph the vehicle damage, the positions of all vehicles, road markings and conditions, and the weather. Note the time and location. Collect the names, addresses, insurance and registration details of all parties, and the contact details of any witnesses. This evidence is invaluable if there is a later dispute over what happened.

faq.q: Should I admit fault after an accident?
faq.a: No. Never admit fault at the scene, even if you think you may be to blame. Stick to stating the facts of what happened when exchanging details and reporting to the police and your insurer. Liability is determined later based on evidence, and an on-the-spot admission can complicate or prejudice your claim.
